raw_response:
I am old now, and with only 6 mu and two people in the house, I cannot spread myself too wide. I have farmed here in Quzhou for 50 years, so I still trust what I have seen on my own land most of all. Wheat and maize are my main insurance because grain is steady and I know the management well. Cotton can make money in a good year, but it takes more watching and more hand labor, so I will not put too much land into it. This year I will keep 4 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation and leave 2 mu for cotton. I have a well, so I am not fully dependent on rain, but pumping water costs money, so I only irrigate at the key times. With my age and small household, I will do mostly the same as last year, just not too aggressive on inputs. I would rather use a little more fertilizer on wheat than risk weak growth, but I will not chase very high yield because cash and labor are both tight.

For wheat, I will sow in early October on the 4 mu that goes into the wheat-maize cycle. I usually use a local improved variety from the township dealer, put most fertilizer down before sowing, then topdress once around jointing if the stand looks a bit light. Wheat is still the crop I trust most, so I will give it a steadier input. After harvest in June, I will rush in summer maize on the same 4 mu. The turnaround is always tight here, so I will keep tillage simple and plant fast after wheat harvest. For maize, I do not want too much fertilizer in one shot because if rain does not come right, it is wasted, so I split it. Cotton will stay on 2 mu only. Cotton can bring cash, but at my age it is more troublesome, with more pest watching and more labor for picking, so I keep it smaller and manage it carefully rather than expanding it.
